This alpha build may trigger a platform warning. One Link does not yet publish a verified, platform-code-signed release. Treat an unverified binary as untrusted; source availability alone does not authenticate the bytes you ran.

Why did the platform warn me?

The project has not yet published a production release with platform code signing, notarization, exact-tag Sigstore bundles, provenance, and a complete SBOM. A warning is therefore expected for some local development builds, but it is not evidence that a binary is safe.

Code-signed installers remain a release goal. Until immutable release evidence exists, evaluate only a reviewed source commit with the frozen lock, or independently verify every artifact against its exact tag.

You can inventory every installed package file locally with one-link verify-this-install --inventory-only, but local hashes alone do not prove authenticity. A verified release must supply an independently authenticated rollup for --expected-rollup and an exact-tag Sigstore bundle; wildcard publisher identities are never accepted.

Sharing behavior
Private by default
Read receipts and typing indicators are under your control.

On: paired devices skip the per-capability prompt and get full access. Off: you approve each new pairing's reach. Trust costs nothing until it does.

Encrypts your local database at rest. Set the ONE_LINK_PASSPHRASE environment variable before launching One Link. It's a 2014 vibe, but it works.

Read receipts

On: peers see ✓✓ once you've actually read their message. Off: peers never learn what you've read. They'll cope.

Off: your sent messages stay at ✓ no matter what. Useful if "Read" lives rent-free in your head.

Typing indicators

On: peers see the little dots while you compose. Off: peers wonder. We think wondering is a feature.

Off: the typing banner never appears, no matter how furiously someone is typing at you.

Blocked devices

Blocked devices can't pair, send, or vibe in your direction. Unblock here if you've forgiven them.

Nobody on the list. Yet.

Active browser sessions

Local-only sign-in receipts. Stored in state.db on this device, never sent over the internet. Each row below is one browser. Click Revoke on any one you don't recognize.

Loading sessions…

On: a revocable credential scoped to this exact browser origin keeps you signed in after daemon restarts. Off: every restart sends you back to opening from the tray icon (no persistent browser credential or session table). Turning this off wipes the whole sessions table immediately.

On: rows above say "Edge on Windows" so you can tell browsers apart. Off: rows show only the session id + last-used time. Turning this off strips browser fingerprints from every existing row in the same write.

Notifications

System notifications from your browser. If you've muted a specific device in its drawer, that mute always wins - you won't get a notification from a muted device even when this is on.

What to notify about

Include message text in the desktop notification. Off if your lock screen is read by people you didn't invite.

Pings when a peer adds or removes an emoji on something you said. Off if you don't need to know who 👍'd what.

Sound
Do-not-disturb

During quiet hours, notifications and chimes shut up. Messages still arrive; they just don't make a scene. Crosses midnight (e.g. 22:00 → 07:00).

Storage & data

Downloads

Files land here. Leave blank for the built-in inbox. Pick a folder that already exists and is writable.

Default disappearing messages

Applies to NEW devices you pair from here on. Existing chats keep whatever TTL is on their device drawer; we don't time-travel into old conversations.

Bandwidth limit

Caps One Link's combined send + receive throughput. Useful on a metered connection, or if you'd like the rest of the internet to keep working.

Incoming files

On (recommended): private file sends from someone you've paired with wait for your OK before they land. Off: they download automatically. Either way, conversational content (screenshots and small inline images pasted in chat) auto-accepts so a casual back-and-forth never gets stuck on a prompt, and shared folders you've explicitly chosen sync without asking.

Auto-accept files

Inbound files that pass these rules land in your inbox quietly. Anything outside (too big, or extension not in the allowlist) gets bounced. Sorry, we have standards (you set them).

Clear app traces

These actions erase One Link's local records only. They do not delete files or folders from your computer, and they do not revoke your identity or paired devices.

The wipe clears chats, file-transfer records, folder metadata, activity/audit rows, route memory, and local UI trace settings. Actual files stay where they are.

iPhone first time or network changed? (trust setup)

iOS won't let Safari bypass a self-signed cert warning on a LAN address. Install the removable trust profile below. Its authority is constrained to this laptop's One Link names and current local addresses; it cannot authenticate arbitrary public websites. If the laptop's address changes, install the newly generated profile before pairing again.

  1. Scan the trust-profile QR below, or copy the URL.
  2. When iOS asks to download a configuration profile, tap Allow.
  3. Open Settings - General - VPN & Device Management, then install One Link Trust.
  4. Open Settings - General - About - Certificate Trust Settings, then trust One Link Root CA.
  5. Scan the pair QR above.

Advanced

Operator controls for diagnostics, runtime support bundles, deep health checks, and truth-status inspection.

Log verbosity

Affects One Link's terminal log + the diagnostics overlay. "Debug" surfaces every wire frame and CRDT merge. Useful when something is misbehaving; noisy otherwise.

Troubleshooting

Live error log + a health check. Open this only if something feels off. In normal use you'll never need it, which is the dream.

Share a diagnostic snapshot

Build a minimal report with build versions, aggregate device and transfer counters, boolean settings, and error totals by fixed category. Freeform logs, names, fingerprints, messages, paths, addresses, user-agent data, and exact timestamps are never added. Review the JSON before sharing it.

One Link Doctor

Quick health check across every surface that has to work for messages, files, and calls. Tells you what's healthy, what's degraded, and what to do.

Protocol ...
Schema ...

One Link is peer-to-peer chat + file sync, end-to-end encrypted by default. No account or central message store is required, and One Link sends no product analytics. Optional rendezvous discovers routes; an optional relay may carry ciphertext but cannot decrypt message or file content.

Built on Coherence; yes, we drank our own kool-aid. Source on GitHub

If something feels wrong

Open a bug report on GitHub. The link opens in a new tab; once it's open use the "Copy report" button above to grab a sanitized diagnostic bundle you can paste into the issue. We never know anything about bugs you don't tell us about.

Report a bug on GitHub

Updates

One Link checks GitHub Releases for newer version tags according to your sovereignty mode. A manual “Install verified update” action appears in the update notice only for a completely validated frozen standalone bundle; its external helper performs full-application rollback and post-restart health checks. Unattended/background installation is not available.

Folder sync conflicts

Two devices changed the same file at the same time. Pick which version wins for each file. Choosing "Keep both" preserves your version under its original name AND saves the other device's version with a .conflict-<peer> suffix so nothing is lost.

No conflicts. Everyone agrees, for once. ✓

Sync settings

Folder location

The folder on this computer that One Link mirrors. Move or rename it from inside One Link instead of from your file manager so the watcher stays attached.

Skip these files + folders

Glob patterns, one per line. Anything that matches gets left out of sync. node_modules/ excludes that directory, *.log excludes log files anywhere.

If both devices change the same file

When you and a paired device edit the same file at the same time, pick which version One Link keeps. You can change this later, and the Conflicts banner lets you override per file.

Send folder

One-shot copy to the selected device. No ongoing sync, no future edits propagate. Cancel any time before or during.

Reach devices across the internet?

One Link finds devices on the same Wi-Fi network or wired local network without infrastructure. That is usually all a household needs.

To reach devices in other locations (a laptop at home from a coffee shop, family across town), configure a rendezvous meeting point so devices can exchange signed reachability records. If no direct route works, an optional relay can carry end-to-end encrypted payloads; it never gets the keys needed to read them.

How to set one up (advanced)
  • Use a rendezvous a friend or community is running - paste their URL into Settings → Rendezvous URLs.
  • Run your own - free, ~5 minutes, see RENDEZVOUS_DEPLOY.md in the repo.
